module purpose: neorv32_gptmr is a bus-controlled timer that stores control bits and a 32-bit threshold, selects one clkgen_i bit as a tick source, counts until the count matches the threshold, and latches an interrupt-pending flag. It returns control, threshold, count, and pending status on bus_rsp_o, exports the enable state on clkgen_en_o, and drives irq_o from irq_pnd.

use-case flows.value: timer enable and tick-source selection written into the control register
32-bit threshold value written into the threshold register
selected clock ticks advancing or clearing the timer count and generating a threshold match
one-cycle interrupt-clear command written from the control word and applied to the pending interrupt state
interrupt pending status set on threshold match and driven to irq_o
stored control bits, threshold, current count, and pending interrupt status returned on addressed reads
control, threshold, tick, count, clear command, pending interrupt state, and bus response forced to known zero values while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Timer enable state -- whether counting and interrupt generation are active
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes the enable bit into ctrl at line 76 after the addressed write checks at lines 73-75, and reset clears ctrl at line 63. The stored value is exported on clkgen_en_o at line 106 and directly controls operation: line 118 forces timer.count to zero when the bit is 0, while lines 141-148 only allow irq_pnd to be set or retained when the bit is 1. Integrity is therefore established for both counting and interrupt behavior; availability is also established because the bit is held in ctrl and leaves the entity on clkgen_en_o. Its bus-write entry point is bus_req_i, a transport record, so only the internal store and scalar exit are listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Timer tick-source selection -- which clkgen_i bit is sampled as the timer tick
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes the three selection bits into ctrl at lines 77-79, and line 117 uses those stored bits to index clkgen_i for timer.tick. Integrity is established because a wrong stored selection captures the wrong clkgen_i bit and changes the timer counting rate and the timing of threshold match and interrupt generation. Availability is also established because the selection is held in ctrl until reset or rewrite, with reset clearing ctrl at line 63. The writing port is the excluded transport record bus_req_i, so ctrl is the listed realization point.

conceptual assets.concept: Timer threshold value -- the 32-bit limit used for match and rollover
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes timer.thres from the addressed bus word at lines 83-84, and addressed reads return it at line 96. The operate and report flows depend on the exact value because line 131 compares timer.count with timer.thres to form timer.match, which then drives counter rollover at lines 121-124 and interrupt assertion at line 142. Integrity is established because a corrupted threshold changes when rollover and interrupt generation occur; availability is also established because the value is stored and can be read back, although bus_rsp_o is a transport record and is not listed as a structural exit.

conceptual assets.concept: Current timer count -- the 32-bit state advanced on selected ticks
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow updates timer.count according to the programmed rules: line 119 clears it when the timer is disabled, line 122 clears it on a matching tick, and line 124 increments it otherwise when timer.tick is 1 at line 120. The current value is returned on addressed reads at line 98 and is compared against the threshold at line 131. Integrity is established because corruption breaks both the reported count and the timing of threshold match and interrupt generation; availability is also established because the register holds and updates the count under those RTL-visible conditions. bus_rsp_o is a transport record, so only the stored register is listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Threshold-match decision -- whether the current count equals the programmed threshold
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 131 computes timer.match from the relation between timer.count and timer.thres. That decision controls whether the counter rolls over or increments at lines 121-124 and whether irq_pnd is set at line 142, so Integrity is established for both the operate flow and the interrupt report flow. Availability is also established because the comparison result is continuously produced from the current count and threshold.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt-clear command -- the one-cycle request to drop the pending interrupt
conceptual assets.reasoning: bus_access captures the clear command in irq_clr at line 81 and also forces irq_clr back to 0 each cycle at line 71, with reset clearing it at line 65, so the RTL implements a one-cycle command rather than a held setting. irq_generator consumes that command at lines 144-145 to clear irq_pnd when the timer is enabled and when no simultaneous timer.match at line 142 takes priority. Integrity is established because a spurious or missing clear changes the implemented interrupt-handling behavior; availability is also established because the command is captured on the addressed write that produces it.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt pending status -- whether the timer has raised an interrupt request
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_generator stores irq_pnd as the module's interrupt state: line 143 sets it on timer.match while enabled, line 145 clears it on irq_clr in the non-match case, and line 148 clears it when the timer is disabled, with reset clearing it at line 139. The report flow exposes this state in control readback at line 94 and drives it out on irq_o at line 154. Integrity is established because both the reported status and irq_o must reflect the RTL-defined pending condition; availability is also established because the state is raised and retained until one of the defined clear cases occurs. bus_rsp_o is a transport record and is therefore not listed as a structural exit.
